items.explanation_en: Open personal rating: no fixed key; score each of the ten factors from 1 to 5, then compare priorities with your partner.
items.draft_answer: I would give a 5 to 'whether the job aligns with my interest' and 'whether the job is compatible with my personality', because I know I would lose motivation in work I do not care about. Pay and job security would get a 4, since I still have to support myself after graduation. Location and corporate culture would be 3: they matter, but they are not decisive for me.

items.explanation_en: Open discussion: name the factor(s) you scored highest in Activity 1 and justify the choice with a personal reason or example.
items.draft_answer: The factor I value most is interest, because Text A shows that people who enjoy their work are happier, less stressed and more satisfied with their lives. I would rather accept a modest salary in a field I find meaningful than a well-paid job I dread every morning. Income still matters to me, but it is a condition for living, not the purpose of working.

items.explanation_en: Open discussion: describe a job that satisfies both your own interest and a real social need, and explain the link between them.
items.draft_answer: I would like to be a special-education teacher, because I enjoy working with children and explaining things patiently. The job also meets a real social need, since many children with learning difficulties lack trained support. The pay is not high, but as Text A says, a job that is both useful to society and personally fulfilling gives you a lasting sense of purpose and enthusiasm.

items.explanation_en: Para. 1 states the thesis directly: 'To be truly happy a person must feel both free and important'; compulsion and being ignored both destroy happiness.
Paras. 2-3: play is a 'purely private pastime' that society does not care about, while labor is compulsory work that earns revenue and meets societal expectations.
Para. 3: the label depends 'not on the job itself, but on the tastes of the individual', not on manual versus mental work or on income.
Para. 4: to workers leisure is only the rest hours needed to 'work efficiently'; to laborers it 'means autonomy from compulsion', the time they value most.
Para. 5: workers who enjoy their jobs are 'happier, less stressed, and generally more satisfied', whereas laborers see the 'daily grind' as wasted time.
Para. 6: innovation and the division of labor remove the need for special skills and turn 'paid occupations with enjoyable work into boring labor'.
Para. 7 rejects the 'toxic attitude' and recommends lifelong learning, 'continuing education' and 'experiential learning' to improve the mind and working conditions.
Para. 8 uses the phrase to show that even 'purely mental work can suffice as an outlet' for people who hurl their passion into a problem.
Open discussion: go beyond dedication and list other traits of people who love their jobs, supporting each trait with a reason or example.
items.draft_answer: Apart from dedication, people who love their jobs tend to be curious and willing to keep learning, which Text A links to lifelong learning and 'experiential learning'. They also take visible pride in what they produce, as the shoe repairer in Text B does, and they are generous with colleagues rather than complaining about them. Finally, they enjoy the process and not only the reward, which is why time passes quickly for them at work.

items.explanation_en: Open discussion: suggest practical ways to move from labor to work, such as matching interests, building pride, and learning in leisure time.
items.draft_answer: One way is to find the part of the job that matches your interests and put more energy there, since the label depends on the individual's tastes rather than on the job itself. Another is to build pride in the work by doing each task properly, as the shoe repairer's father advised. Using leisure time for continuing education can also turn a boring routine into something you understand, and therefore enjoy.

items.explanation_en: Open discussion: describe realistic responses to job dissatisfaction, such as changing your attitude, retraining, or moving to work that fits.
items.draft_answer: First I would ask whether the problem is the job or my attitude toward it, since the author insists that people's attitude toward their work 'determines everything'. If the work itself is the problem, I would use my spare time to learn new skills and prepare for a change, as Text A recommends. Before leaving, though, I would talk to my manager about taking on new challenges, because getting bored is one of the main reasons people switch jobs.

items.explanation_en: The infinitive after 'to' needs a base verb; 'gauge' means to measure or estimate how much line is needed.
The past tense is set by 'ultimately finished'; 'contend for' means to compete for a prize or position.
'Fairly' takes a gradable adjective, and 'commonplace' fits 'on commuter trains', meaning very common there.
'Will' is followed by the base verb; 'suffice to do sth' means to be enough to achieve it.
The possessive 'the company's' needs a noun; 'revenue' is the income a company generates from sales.
'Adverse' collocates with 'effects' and matches the negative impact of human activities on the environment and climate.
'Upcoming' modifies 'exam' as the exam that is about to take place.
'Will be' requires a past participle for the passive; 'abolish' means to officially end a program or practice.
The article 'a' plus the adjective 'pleasant' needs a noun; 'diversion' is an enjoyable distraction or pastime.
'Will' takes the base verb, and 'foster interest in' is the collocation meaning to encourage interest to grow.
'Law enforcement' is a fixed compound naming the police and the work they do.
'Ready for shipment' is the standard phrase for goods about to be transported to a new home.
The ban aims to stop the collection being turned into a business, which is exactly 'commercialism'.
'Magical realism' is the literary term for a realistic world in which fantastical elements are treated as normal.
'Recruitment fair' is the fixed term for an event connecting job-seekers with employers.
The sentence describes Rome's expansionist policy of conquest, which 'imperialism' names.
'Without' needs a noun parallel to 'complaint'; 'resentment' means bitterness at unfair treatment.
The blank names the phenomenon behind terror attacks, so the abstract noun 'terrorism' is required.
The contrast with generosity and 'spiritual hunger' points to 'materialism', the devotion to money and possessions.
'The ___ that people are happy when they have a good salary' needs a noun for a belief, and 'notion' means an idea or belief.
'Foster a sense of joy' is the collocation; 'foster' means to encourage something to develop.
The blank modifies 'state of mind' and must be a participle: 'reflecting' pictures a deliberately thoughtful, self-aware outlook rather than a passive one.
'Monetary rewards' contrasts with 'material gain' later in the same sentence.
'Refrain from doing sth' is the fixed pattern, and the gerund 'thinking' follows the blank.
The subject slot before 'about bad things are easy' needs a gerund, and 'complaining' matches the negative tone of the sentence.
'Help and ___ from other people' needs a plural noun; 'incentives' are things that motivate people to act.
'Getting ___' names the feeling that drives people to switch jobs, and boredom is the main cause listed here.
'Exhaustive plans' means very thorough plans, which suits the advice to make and then follow them.
'Hit a barrier' is the collocation for meeting an obstacle, after which help from a manager is welcome.
'Correlate with' expresses a statistical link between the rise in unemployment and the increase in young people living at home.
'Can't refrain from doing sth' means cannot stop oneself; 'from' is followed by the gerund 'hugging'.
'Be counting down the days' means to wait eagerly for an event, which fits the promise that they will come.
After 'spend time' the -ing form is required; 'slaving away' means working extremely hard for years.
'Can't wait to do sth' takes the infinitive, and 'sink one's teeth into' means to become fully absorbed in a task.
'Must contend with' means have to deal with a difficulty, here an unfamiliar environment.
The passive 'be designated as' means be officially named for a role, here distance learning teacher.
The verb is parallel to 'meets' and agrees with singular 'cooperation'; 'conform to' means to comply with.
Structure analysis task: identify the general statement opening each paragraph and the point-by-point pattern, not a fixed answer.
items.draft_answer: Paragraph 4 opens with the general statement that workers and laborers can be told apart by their attitude toward leisure, and paragraph 5 with the equally general claim that they differ in the personal satisfaction they get from their jobs. Each paragraph then contrasts the two groups point by point on the very same aspect: leisure as rest versus autonomy from compulsion, and pride and satisfaction versus a wasted daily grind. This point-by-point pattern, rather than block-by-block, keeps the two categories side by side, so the contrast between them stays sharp for the reader.

items.explanation_en: Essay task: no single answer; follow the outline of thesis, three points of comparison and conclusion in at least 140 words.
items.draft_answer: Deciding whether to continue studying or start working comes down to whether you need depth or experience first. Graduate study gives you specialized training and protected time to think, which matters in fields like research or medicine, while starting work early brings a salary, real projects and skills no classroom can teach. A degree opens some doors, and work experience builds the judgment and network that employers also value. My own view is that the right choice depends on your field and on how clearly you know your goal, and that either path should be chosen deliberately rather than by default.

items.explanation_en: 'For I was rushing to meet a friend' gives the cause of her impatience, and 'because' in the same paragraph explains the worn heel, so both signal cause.
'Thereafter', 'At first' and 'Then' mark successive stages of the friendship, so they signal time order rather than cause or contrast.
'Then' continues the sequence; 'No matter what' concedes a point, 'if' sets a condition, and 'When' marks the time of the change.
Para. 1: 'I rushed into his little shop to have the heels of my shoes repaired', which option B restates.
Para. 4 gives the reason directly: 'I grew a little impatient, for I was rushing to meet a friend.'
Para. 6 calls the claim 'a bit absurd' for 'this modest little shop', so her first reaction was doubt, not confusion or upset.
Para. 7 quotes the father: 'do the best job on every shoe... and be proud of your fine work', which is dedication plus pride.
Para. 10: she dropped in 'just to chat with him for the joy he would impart', so it was the pleasure his company gave her.
Para. 12 shows him singing in the doorway as the children's favourite; the other three statements are never made in the text.
Para. 13: he says the painters' parents 'had no pride in their work', so what they lacked was a prideful tradition.
The closing lines state his wisdom: 'If you have inherited a prideful tradition, you must carry it on; if you haven't, then start building one now.'
Open discussion: interpret the image of society as fabric and say what a good contribution means for ordinary jobs.
items.draft_answer: I read it as meaning that society is woven from countless small jobs, so every worker leaves a thread in it, whether as a cobbler, a teacher or a cleaner. The point is not that all contributions are equal in status but that each can be done well or badly. His own answer is to do the best job on every shoe, so the fabric holds because ordinary people take pride in ordinary tasks.

items.explanation_en: Open discussion: identify factors behind pride in work, such as craftsmanship, recognition, autonomy and fair pay, and support them.
items.draft_answer: The clearest factor is craftsmanship: the shoe repairer is proud because he uses good leather and stitches each pair properly. Recognition matters too, since pride grows when customers and managers notice good work, and autonomy helps people feel the result is truly theirs. Fair pay and training also contribute, because pride is hard to sustain when work is badly rewarded or nobody has taught you how to do it well.

items.explanation_en: Open discussion: take a position on passing down inherited traditions and support it with reasons or examples.
items.draft_answer: Yes, but selectively: what is worth handing down is the skill and the standard behind a tradition, not every detail of how it was once practised. The glassware artist in Text C hopes her art will pass 'from one generation to another' because it is beautiful and represents a high level of skill, yet she has only her two sons to teach. Keeping such crafts alive preserves knowledge, but young people should be free to adapt them rather than simply copy them.

items.explanation_en: 'Unhappy laborer' is the counterpart of 'happy worker', echoing Text A's contrast between laborers and workers.
After 'finds her work' a complement is needed; 'personally fulfilling' means the work satisfies her as a person.
'Can always ___' needs a verb phrase, so the blank is 'find optimum pleasure', echoing Text A's 'taking optimum pleasure in the task at hand'.
The initial 'l' and the sense of trying to bring something about point to 'learn', i.e. companies try to learn how to create a happy workplace.
The list 'things like ___, free gym membership, or health care' needs a benefit noun, and 'monetary rewards' fits beside those material perks.
'For the sake of doing sth' is the fixed phrase, and here it describes working only to earn a living.
'Which bring you ___' after 'create value' needs 'personal satisfaction', the reward Text A also ties to work.
The contrast with 'a key source of happiness' calls for 'trivial task', the small ordinary acts that still satisfy people.
'Praising and recognizing ___' is completed by 'specific results', the concrete achievements colleagues can point to.
The contrast with 'impressive performance' requires 'high position': recognition should come from work, not from rank.
'Seem like ___' needs a plural noun, and 'polar opposites' restates the labor-versus-play contrast of Text A.
With the initial 'fi' and the following 'grab a coffee', the intended phrase is 'finished task'.
With the initial 'ch', 'cheerful smile' fits, the very greeting the cobbler gives the author in Text B.
'Have an ___ on' is completed by 'adverse effect', the collocation Text A uses for harmful influence.
Key renderings: 'place higher demands on', 'confine themselves to', 'take an active part in', 'sense of social responsibility', 'clarify the direction of future efforts'.
